newsitem.title: USA: Reich says US must focus on narrowing earning gap.
newsitem.headline: Reich says US must focus on narrowing earning gap.

text.p: The United States should make the narrowing of the earnings gap a major economic priority, outgoing Labor Secretary Robert Reich said in his final speech as a cabinet member on Thursday.
Reich said that the gap in real earnings has been slowly widening for more than 15 years and that the government and the public must work together to end that trend.
"We can not retreat into gated communities," Reich said. "There is no place to hide."

Reich, who has spoken repeatedly about the income gap during his four-year tenure as Labor Secretary, said the earnings disparity is not just based on pay, but also on a gap in benefits, such as health care and pensions, and in education opportunities.
"America is prospering, but the prosperity is not being widely shared, certainly not as widely shared as it once was," he said.

The secretary has not decided what he will do after he leaves his cabinet post next week, a spokeswoman said. Reich, who was on the faculty of Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government before coming to the Labor Department, is exploring teaching options at several universities, she said.
Reich also plans to team up with retired Sen. Alan Simpson to produce a talk show, "The Long and the Short of It." Reich is under five feet tall and Simpson towers at six feet seven inches.
